slides.title: Dating questions you're too shy to ask

slides.q: Is it weird to Google my date before we meet?
slides.a: Not at all, it's actually smart. A quick search helps you confirm they're who they say they are. Just don't go so deep that you show up knowing their whole life story. For first dates, meet somewhere public, tell a friend where you'll be, and get yourself there and home on your own.

slides.q: Is it normal to not want to kiss on a first date?
slides.a: Totally normal. Plenty of people need more time to feel comfortable, and a first date is about figuring out if you even like each other. You can end it with a hug or just say you had a good time. Anyone worth seeing again will be fine with that, and not kissing says nothing bad about the date.

slides.q: Is it normal to be nervous having sex with someone new?
slides.a: Completely normal. New partners come with new bodies, new rhythms and a lot of unknowns, so nerves make sense. Talking helps more than people expect: share what you're into, ask what they like, and agree on protection beforehand. Remember you can slow down or stop anytime. It usually gets easier as trust builds.

slides.q: Is it normal to fart in front of your partner?
slides.a: Yes, and it's going to happen eventually anyway. Most people pass gas several times a day, it's just digestion. Some couples laugh about it from day one, others take a while to get comfortable, and both are fine. Worth seeing a doctor if gas comes with ongoing pain, bloating or big changes in your bathroom habits.

slides.q: How do I meet people without dating apps?
slides.a: Put yourself where people with your interests already are: run clubs, classes, volunteering, rec sports, trivia nights. Lots of couples still meet through friends, so tell yours you're open to being set up. Going to the same places regularly helps, since familiarity makes it easier to start talking. Just saying hi more often counts too.
